acceptance_criteria.name: early_adaptation_no_deficit
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, candidate successes at B1 checkpoint 8 >= recent8 successes at B1 checkpoint 8, AND candidate successes at B2 checkpoint 8 >= recent8 successes at B2 checkpoint 8 (96 tasks per figure). Evaluated separately on the development and additional cohorts.

acceptance_criteria.name: harm_never_worse_than_recent8
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, at EVERY checkpoint of B1, return_A, and B2 (including checkpoint 0), candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions at the same checkpoint. Any single checkpoint violation fails this criterion for that cohort. Checkpoint-0 (onset) harm is additionally reported in the experiment report.

acceptance_criteria.name: retention_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, candidate successes at return_A checkpoint 8 >= ceil(0.90 * frozen_A successes at return_A checkpoint 8).

acceptance_criteria.name: abstention_budget
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, candidate failed-by-abstention <= 24 of 96 tasks at checkpoint 8 of each of B1, return_A, and B2. Abstentions are never counted as successes at any checkpoint.

acceptance_criteria.name: no_false_reversion
acceptance_criteria.rule: Three parts, all required, per cohort: (a) at B1-64 and B2-64 the candidate's recorded selection is not the archive for any seed; (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 8 of 96 at B1-64 and <= 8 of 96 at B2-64; (c) stationary control arm: across the 18 seed-checkpoints at k in {2,4,8,16,32,64} (3 seeds x 6 checkpoints), the candidate selects the archive in at least 17, i.e. false-reversion count <= 1.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), and per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions for every method at every checkpoint. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

baselines.name: recent8
baselines.role: Simplest credible baseline and documented early-phase champion: relation model on the last 8 observed events only.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint; criterion 5 harm comparison
baselines.name: recent32
baselines.role: Relation model on the last 32 observed events.

baselines.in: criterion 3 retention reference; reported at every checkpoint
baselines.name: frozen_A
baselines.role: Relation model fitted on the first 192 events, never updated (same fit as the candidate archive, without selection or gating).

baselines.name: cumulative
baselines.role: Relation model on all observed events.

baselines.name: always_abstain
baselines.role: Abstains on every TEST task: 0 successes, 0 harmful actions, all tasks failed-by-abstention.

baselines.name: untrained_random
baselines.role: Independent seeded random TEST action policy; gathers no training outcomes.

baselines.in: reported at every checkpoint, labeled privileged
baselines.name: privileged_expected_oracle
baselines.role: PRIVILEGED reference only: knows the expected hidden rule (not the realized stochastic flip). Never a realizable baseline and never counted in any PASS/FAIL comparison.

boundaries: No privileged simulator information to the learner; the oracle is a labeled reference only.
No learner-issued training interventions; all TRAIN evidence comes from the shared external actor stream.
No default controller promotion, no PR merge, no D1-D10 or V2A/V2B roadmap change, no AthenZ/Synveil integration (hard gates requiring the owner's explicit authorization).
Same engineered two-feature simulator family as the preceding switch experiments; results are not evidence of independent generalization, novel rule discovery, or real-world safety.
Preserve all negative results with the same prominence as positive ones.

budgets.abstention_budget: Criterion 4: failed-by-abstention <= 24 of 96 tasks (25%) at each 8-observation checkpoint, per stage, per cohort.
budgets.harm_budget: Criteria 2 and 5: candidate harmful TEST actions never exceed recent8 at any checkpoint, and <= 8 of 96 at each B-64 checkpoint, per cohort.
budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 6). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.

expected_failure_modes: Margin too sticky: the archive survives the first B observations on accumulated A evidence and B1-8/B2-8 successes fall below recent-8 (criterion 1 FAIL) with high onset harm (criterion 2 FAIL).
Contradiction override too weak under 1/8 outcome flips and 1/20 report flips: genuinely reversed evidence may not produce 2 sub-0.125 archive probabilities in the latest 4 events.
Adequacy gate too strict under stochastic feedback: abstentions exceed the 25% budget at 8-observation checkpoints (criterion 4 FAIL) while adding no harm protection.
Adequacy gate too lax: the candidate acts on a poorly fitting model and matches the historical onset-harm pattern.
Late false reselection: after 32-64 B observations the archive wins the scoring tail by noise and is reselected, reproducing the REGRET_SWITCH B-64 harm pattern (criterion 5 FAIL).
Return-A failure: recent windows keep winning by the margin on return-A evidence and retained A knowledge is not recovered (criterion 3 FAIL).

fixed_parameters.action_scoring: The selected candidate scores each public action with the existing utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, exactly as RelationOutcomeMemory.choose.
fixed_parameters.adequacy_gate: If the SELECTED candidate's mean prequential log-score over the 8 scoring events is below -1.2 (total below -9.6), the learner abstains from the TEST action. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.archive_definition: A relation model (existing RelationOutcomeMemory estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, k=5 nearest neighbours, 0.05 Laplace smoothing) fitted once on the FIRST 192 public TRAIN events. It is never refitted, extended, or overwritten by later events for the life of the experiment.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce selections identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.contradiction_override: If at least 2 of the latest 4 scoring events have archive-assigned probability < 0.125 for their reported outcome class, the archive is ineligible at that decision regardless of the margin rule; the better recent window (per the recent32-vs-recent8 margin rule above) is selected.
fixed_parameters.prequential_scoring: For each of the last 8 observed events at index i, every candidate is fitted ONLY on events strictly before i (archive: events[0:192]; recent8: events[i-8:i]; recent32: events[i-32:i]) and scored by the natural log probability it assigns to event i's REPORTED outcome class (progress/damage/neutral). Scores are summed over the 8 scoring events. No scored event is ever in its own scoring model (strictly disjoint fit/score evidence).
fixed_parameters.selection_rule: Default selection is the archive. A recent window displaces the archive only if its total prequential log-score exceeds the archive's by MORE than 1.0. Between recent8 and recent32, recent32 is selected only if its total exceeds recent8's by MORE than 1.0; otherwise recent8. There is no separate return-to-A logic: the archive is re-selected by the same rule whenever recent windows no longer beat it by the margin.

candidate.hypothesis: An immutable pre-switch archive protected by an asymmetric displacement margin (a recent window must clearly OUT-predict the archive on strictly prequential evidence before it may displace it), combined with a fast contradiction override (so a genuinely reversed rule is not waited out) and an explicit adequacy gate (abstain rather than act when even the best candidate predicts the recent evidence poorly), will match recent-8 in the first 8 post-switch observations without the archive-forgetting of windows or the late false reselection seen in REGRET_SWITCH.
candidate.name: GatedArchivePrequentialMemory
candidate.placement: New separate optional learner class in developmental_ai/. The default controller and every existing learner are untouched; existing learners appear only as baselines.

capability_under_test: Early-phase behavior after an unannounced rule change: the first 0-8 new observations after a switch. Specifically, whether one retained-knowledge mechanism can simultaneously (i) recover task success as fast as the trivial recent-8 window, (ii) avoid acting on obsolete knowledge, and (iii) preserve the pre-switch knowledge for a later return to the original rule.

checkpoints.note: A checkpoint value k means the learner has observed the full A history plus the first k TRAIN events of the named stage (control: first k continuation events). return_A has only 48 TRAIN events, so its final checkpoint is 48 instead of 64.

cohorts.novelty_statement: Both cohorts are NEW and uninspected as of this freeze. They are disjoint from every cohort in the inspected records, including 17/23/41, 1009/1013/1031, 2749/6607/9901, 14003/14009/14033, 15101/22003/31013, 17431/24869/37021, 27007/27011/27017, 43103/50021/61031, 72019/83003/94009, and the full X2/X3 seed families 112003-113041, 122003-123041, 132003-133041, 142003-143041, 152003-153041, 162003-163041, 172003-173041, 182003-183041, 192003-193041, 202003-203041, 212003-213041, 222003-223041, 232003-233041, 242003-243041, 252003-253041, 262003-263041, 272003-273041, 282003-283041. Disjointness was verified by searching all protocol JSONs, benchmark code, and docs in projects/developmental-ai/ for the six seed values before this commit; none occurred. Both cohorts become INSPECTED once evaluated under this protocol.

grading.ci_claims: Linux/Windows validation is claimed only for an exact commit with a real GitHub Actions run on that commit; otherwise it is recorded as UNVERIFIED.
grading.demonstrated: All six criteria PASS on BOTH cohorts, the historical transfer benchmark (benchmarks.transfer_benchmark, unchanged) still passes, and the full unit suite (python -m unittest discover -s tests) passes on the evaluation commit.
grading.failed: Any of criteria 1-3 FAILs on the additional cohort, or criterion 6 FAILs on either cohort.
grading.format: Handoff section 6 report format. Every acceptance criterion above is graded PASS or FAIL individually, per cohort; no failed criterion may be hidden inside an overall positive summary.
grading.generalization_level: At most handoff level 2-3 (choosing among / applying already-supplied representations under a rule change). No level-6 or novel-representation claim is permitted from this experiment: the A/B rules, span statistic, windows, margin, and thresholds are all designer-supplied.
grading.partially_demonstrated: Criteria 1, 2, and 4 PASS on both cohorts but criterion 3 or 5 FAILs, or all criteria PASS on the development cohort only.
grading.regression: The candidate is worse than recent8 on criterion 1 or 2 on both cohorts, or the historical transfer benchmark or full unit suite breaks.

limitation_evidence: SAME_SCHEMA_SWITCH (docs/SAME_SCHEMA_SWITCH.md): at switch onset 180/180 harmful TEST actions; adaptive B8 0/180 successes vs recent-8 167/180; B64 regression 178/180 vs recent-32 180/180.
FAST_REACQUISITION (benchmarks/fast_reacquisition_protocol.json, inspected cohorts 122003-family / 123001-family): consistency filter B-4 0/180, B-8 26/180 vs recent-8 159/180.
MULTI_SWITCH (benchmarks/multi_switch_protocol.json, 10% corrupted reports): B2 onset 120/120 harmful; preregistered return-A8 gate failed (80/120 vs >=100/120 required).
STOCHASTIC_PREQUENTIAL (benchmarks/stochastic_prequential_protocol.json): B1-8 10/96 and B2-8 15/96 for archived/ensemble methods vs recent-8 47/96 and 57/96.

REGRET_SWITCH (benchmarks/regret_switch_protocol.json): four registered thresholds failed (B2-8, return-A8, B1-32, B2-32); late false reselection of the archived A model caused 56/96 harmful TEST actions at B-64.

VALIDATED_ABSTENTION: harm was reduced to zero only by abstaining on 96/96 tasks (zero completed); TWO_WINDOW agreement8 scored 0/360 on switched stages, all abstentions. Abstention alone is not adaptation.

REGIME_RETRIEVAL: retrieved archive scored 360/360/360 with 0 TEST harms at the 160-observation scale, while recent-32 return-A scored 1/360 with 359 harms: windows adapt fast but forget; archives retain but adapt dangerously slowly at switch onset.
metrics_reported: Per seed, per stage (B1, return_A, B2, control), per checkpoint, per method: successes, harmful TEST actions, failed-by-abstention count, attempted tasks.
Candidate selection (archive / recent8 / recent32 / abstained-by-gate) at every checkpoint, per seed.
Onset harm: harmful TEST actions at checkpoint 0 for every stage, per seed and method, reported explicitly and never pooled away.
Per seed TRAIN accounting, counted once regardless of checkpoints or methods: actor actions, actual harmful actions, actual productive, actual neutral, reported harmful, report label flips.
Learner-issued information-acquisition actions (frozen at 0) and any additional observations requested (frozen at 0).
Checkpoint record SHA256 and restore-replay identity for the candidate.
No pooled-only reporting: every cohort figure must be decomposable into its three per-seed rows.
permitted_observations: The learner sees only the public reported stream of {features, progress, damage} events in chronological order, identical for every method, plus the public TEST frame (actions with public features) at decision time. No phase label, rule identity, episode index, true (unflipped) outcome, report-flip flag, simulator state, or TEST outcome may enter the learner, its selection, or its checkpoint record.
priority: MUSE_BUILD_ORDER Priority 1 (Independent Learning), items 3 (prevent new learning from overwriting established knowledge) and 4 (improve adaptation to changing environments); item 2 (retention) is measured by the return-A stage.
registration: This protocol is committed BEFORE any candidate implementation, unit test, benchmark harness, or score inspection for this experiment. Once either cohort is evaluated, its seeds are INSPECTED: no parameter, threshold, seed, checkpoint, or acceptance criterion in this file may be revised against those results. A revised hypothesis requires a NEW protocol file and NEW seed cohorts.
required_evaluation_runs: This experiment's frozen benchmark on the development cohort and on the additional cohort, exactly as registered here.
Full unit suite: python -m unittest discover -s tests

simulator.actor: Independent hash-seeded random first-action actor, one action per disposable TRAIN episode, identical stream for every method. The learner issues ZERO training interventions of its own (acquisition budget = 0; see budgets).
simulator.family: StochasticWorld exactly as implemented in benchmarks/stochastic_prequential_benchmark.py (SameSchemaWorld two public numeric features inlet/outlet, anonymous actions, authored span-to-effect bands). No simulator code is changed by this experiment; the benchmark harness for this experiment reuses StochasticWorld and public_train unchanged.
simulator.hidden_rules: Hidden physics schedule per seed: A (original progress/damage mapping) -> B1 (progress/damage inverted) -> return_A (original) -> B2 (inverted). Phase boundaries, phase names, and the active rule are benchmark-private and are never supplied to any learner.
simulator.reported_feedback: An independent sha256 draw on (seed, TRAIN episode index) flips a non-neutral TRAIN reported progress/damage label with probability 1/20, exactly as in public_train. The learner receives only the possibly corrupted public report. Actual actor harm and label flips are counted separately by the benchmark.
simulator.stationary_control_arm: A separate arm per seed with NO rule change: 240 A TRAIN episodes (indices 1000..1239) followed by 64 further A TRAIN episodes (indices 5000..5063, physics original). It measures false reversion: how often the candidate abandons its archive when nothing changed.
simulator.true_stochastic_feedback: Every actual non-neutral simulator action has probability 1/8 of a progress/damage flip, drawn by deterministic sha256 of (seed, split, episode index, action id, tick) exactly as in StochasticWorld._sample_outcome. Neutral outcomes stay neutral. TEST outcomes are the realized stochastic outcomes, not clean deterministic ones.

test.repeated_indices_note: The same TEST indices are re-scored at every checkpoint by every method; checkpoint rows are therefore not independent samples. TEST is read-only: no TEST outcome is ever trained on, and the harness must verify each method's checkpoint record is unchanged after TEST evaluation (contamination check, as in stochastic_prequential_benchmark).

training_indices.control_A_continuation: 5000..5063 (64 episodes, physics original, stationary control arm only)
